properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 27 at 4:11PM PST until November 28 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 6.8 feet
will peak near Noon Saturday morning.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 27 at 4:11PM PST until November 28 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10
feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.2
feet will peak between 11 AM and Noon Saturday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued November 27 at 4:06PM PST until November 28 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog. Some
locations will experience zero visibility for several hours. This
dense fog event will be a Level 4 on a scale of 1 to 5.

* WHERE...Much of central California.

* WHEN...From 8 PM this evening to Noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dense fog will make driving conditions hazardous leading
to a high transportation risk.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Dense fog will resemble that of the past two
days. Low clouds will quickly become dense fog shortly after
sunset. Be aware that dense fog will be widespread by late this
evening, if you are traveling.
properties.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your low beam headlights, and leave plenty
of distance ahead of you. Consider leaving after the dense fog has
gone. Be sure to change your headlights from AUTO to MANUAL, since
automatic headlights will not activate in the dense fog.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 27 at 2:53PM PST until November 28 at 6:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of
13 to 19 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low- lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bayside locations along southern Monterey Bay
including Elkhorn Slough.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through 6 AM Saturday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 5 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM
Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM
Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

* WHERE...Central Siskiyou County. This includes Weed, Gazelle,
Grenada, and Montague.  This includes portions of Interstate 5 and
Highway 97.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Sunday to 1 AM PST Monday.

profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 2:37PM PST until November 28 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low
lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near
shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 7.6 and 7.9 feet MLLW at
the Arena Cove tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From noon to 4 PM PST Saturday. High tide is at 1:15 PM
at the Arena Cove tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be
possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas along the coast including
parks, parking lots, roads, and harbors. Only isolated and
minor impacts are expected.
properties.instruction:

will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and beach
erosion. Large breaking waves can cause injury and wash people

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.
Stay off of rock jetties and sea walls. Waves can suddenly and
quickly move much farther up the beach than expected; stay back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.
